technical-data.invention-title: ANTIDIABETIC PIPERAZINE DERIVATIVES, PROCESSES FOR THEIR PREPARATION AND COMPOSITIONS CONTAINING THEM
DERIVES ANTIDIABETIQUES DE PIPERAZINE, LEURS PROCEDES DE PREPARATION ET COMPOSITIONS LES CONTENANT

abstract.p: The invention relates to novel piperazine derivatives of formula (I) wherein (Z)i, X, N and Ar have the meanings as given in claim 1, and which are of use in the treatment of pathologies associated with insulin-resistance syndrome.

L'invention concerne de nouveaux dérivés de pipérazine représentés par la formule (I) dans laquelle (Z)i, X, n et Ar possèdent les significations énoncées dans la revendication 1. Ces dérivés sont utiles pour traiter des pathologies associées au syndrome de résistance à l'insuline.

description.p: ANTIDIABETIC PIPERAZINE DERIVATIVES, PROCESSES FOR THEIR PREPARATION AND COMPOSITIONS CONTAINING THEM
The present invention relates to novel piperazme derivatives which are of use in the treatment of pathologies associated with msulm-resistance 5 syndrome.
The compounds of the invention have the formula:
0 in which: n represents 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6; X represents 0 or S;

Ar represents an aromatic nucleus chosen from phenyl, 5 pyridyl, pyπmidinyl, benzoxazolyl, benzothiazolyl and benzimidazolyl, the said aromatic nucleus optionally being substituted by one or more radicals chosen from a halogen atom; a (Ci-Cβ) al oxy group; a (Cβ-Cio) aryloxy group; a (Cβ-Cio) aryl (Cι-C3) alkoxy group m which the 0 aryl part is optionally substituted oy halogen, (Cι-C6)alkyl or (Cι-C6) alkoxy; and a (Cι-C6) alkyl group substituted by one or more halogen atoms; i represents 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 ; and each Z group independently represents a halogen atom; 5 as well as their addition salts with pnarmaceutically acceptable bases or acids.
The invention also relates to the solvates of the compounds of formula I .

The term "alkyl" is understood to mean, accord- 30 ing to the invention, a linear or branched hydrocarbon- comprising group. Mention may be made, as example of alkyl groups, of the methyl, ethyl, propyl, n-butyl, isobutyl, sec-butyl, tert-butyl, isoamyl, tert-amyl, sec-amyl, pentyl and hexyl groups. 35 The alkyl parts of the alkoxy and arylalkoxy groups have the same definition as given above for the alkyl group.
Mention may be made, as example of alkyl groups substituted by one or more halogen atoms, of the perfluoroalkyl groups, such as trifluoromethyl or pentafluoroethyl . The aryl group is a mono- or polycyclic aromatic group, preferably mono- or bicyclic, such as phenyl or naphthyl . The same definition is valid for the aryl parts of the aryloxy and arylalkoxy groups.
The halogen atoms are chosen from bromine, fluorine, iodine and chlorine.

When Ar represents substituted phenyl, the phenyl nucleus can carry one, two, three, four or five substituents . However, when Ar represents substituted phenyl, the phenyl nucleus is preferably mono-, di- or trisubstituted. In this case, the substituents are preferably in the meta or para position.
Examples of preferred aryloxy groups are phenoxy and naphthyloxy.
An example of a preferred arylalkoxy group is the benzyloxy group.
The -CH2-COOH group of the compounds of the invention is situated either in the ortho position or m the meta position or in the para position with regard to the chain

However, preference is given to the compounds m which the -CH2-COOH group is in the para or ortho position, the para position being especially preferred. The compounds of formula I have a carboxyl functional group and can be salified. They are then provided in the form of addition salts with organic or inorganic bases. The addition salts with bases are, for example, pharmaceutically acceptable salts, such as the sodium salts, the potassium salts or the calcium salts, which
are obtained by using the corresponding alkali metal or alkaline earth metal hydroxides as bases.
Mention may be made, as other types of addition salts with pharmaceutically acceptable bases, of the salts with amines and n particular glucamme,
N-methylglucamme, N,N-dιmethylglucamme, ethanolamme, morpholme, N-methylmorpholme or lysme.

The compounds of formula I can also be salified with inorganic or organic acids and preferably pharma- ceutically acceptable acids, such as hydrochloric acid, phosphoric acid, fumanc acid, citric acid, oxalic acid, sulphuric acid, ascorbic acid, tartaπc acid, maleic acid, mandelic acid, methanesulphonic acid, lactobionic acid, gluconic acid, glucaπc acid, succimc acid, sulphomc acid or hydroxypropane- sulphomc acid.

The salts of the compounds of formula I with acids and bases which are not pharmaceutically acceptable form another aspect of the invention. These salts are intermediate compounds of use m the preparation of the compounds of the invention. This is because the compounds of the invention can be isolated as intermediates in the form of one of their non- pharmaceutically acceptable salts, before conversion to a pharmaceutically acceptable compound.
A first group of preferred compounds is composed of the compounds of formula I in which X represents an oxygen atom.
Preference is more particularly given, among the compounds of the invention, to those in which n represents 2 or 3 and better still those m which n is 2.

Another group of preferred compounds is composed of the compounds in which Ar represents unsubstituted pyridyl, unsubstituted pyrimidmyl or optionally substituted phenyl. When Ar represents substituted phenyl, the phenyl group preferably carries one or two substituents chosen from (Cι-C6) alkoxy, halogen, phenoxy, tπfluoromethyl and benzyloxy. Better
still, when Ar represents substituted pnenyl, the phenyl group is substituted m the meta position by a (Ci-Cβ) alkoxy group, a phenoxy group, a tπfluoromethyl group or a halogen atom, such as a fluorine or chlorine atom.
Another group of preferred compounds is composed of the compounds of formula I m which I represents 1 or 0, preferably 0.
According to a preferred alternative form of the invention, when i is 1, the -CH2-COOH group is situated in the ortho position with regard to the chain
and the Z substituent is in the para position with respect to this same chain.
A final group of preferred compounds is composed of the compounds of formula I m which the -CH2-COOH group is situated in the para position on the phenyl group with respect to the chain

The invention also relates to two processes for the preparation of the compounds of formula I.
According to a first process, an aromatic compound of formula II:

in which Z, X and I are as defined above for the formula I and Pi is a protective group for a carboxyl
functional group, is reacted with a piperazme of formula III:
m which n and Ar are as defined aoove for the formula I and Grpi is a leaving group.

Among the protective groups for carboxyl functional groups, those generally described in Protective Groups m Organic Synthesis, Greene T.W. and Wuts P.G.M., published by John Wiley and Sons, 1991, and in Protective Groups, Kocienski P.J., 1994, Georg Thieme Verlag, may be suitable. It is possible, by way of example, to envisage the protection of the carboxyl functional group m the ester form: in this case, Pi represents (Cι-C6) alkyl.

A halogen atom (for example chlorine or bromine), a (Cβ-Cio) arylsulphonyloxy group, in which the aryl group is optionally substituted by one or more (Ci-Cδ) alkyl groups, or a (Ci-Cβ) alkylsulphonyloxy group, in which the alkyl group is optionally substituted by one or more halogen atoms, may be selected as example of a Grpi group.
The operating conditions for the reaction of the compound II with the piperazme III will be easily determined by a person skilled m the art, this reaction being a nucleophilic substitution.

The reaction of the compound II with the piperazme III is advantageously carried out m a polar aprotic solvent n the presence of a base. Examples of appropriate solvents are acetonitrile, dimethylformamide, acetone, dimethyl sulphoxide and halogenated hydrocarbons, such as dichloromethane or dichloroethane .

Use may be made, as particularly preferred base, of potassium carbonate.
According to a preferred embodiment, the reaction of II with III is carried out at a temperature of 50 to 120°C, for example at reflux of acetonitrile, when the latter is chosen as solvent, the presence of an alkali metal iodide, such as potassium iodide.

The amount of potassium iodide which has to be used is variable and depends essentially on the nature of the reactants, on tne nature of the solvent and on the reaction temperature. A catalytic amount of potassium iodide (less than 1 molar equivalent with respect to the compound II) is generally sufficient.

The reaction of the compound II with the compound III is stoichiometric. However, it may be possible to carry out the reaction m the presence of a slight excess of the piperazme III, in such a way that the molar ratio of III to II will generally be between 1 and 1.2.
The reaction of the compound II with the piperazme III leads to a compound of formula IV:
in which Pi, X, Z, l, n and Ar are as defined above, which compound is converted to a compound of formula I by deprotection of the carboxyl functional group.

The deprotection methods are those commonly used n the art. They are, for example, described in Protective Groups in Organic Synthesis, Green T.W. and Wuts P.G.M., published by John Wiley and Sons, 1991, and in Protective Groups, Kocienski P.J., 1994, Georg Thieme Verlag.

When Pi represents (Cι-C6) alkyl, the deprotection can involve the saponification of the ester
functional group, for example by the action of dilute sodium hydroxide solution.
The compounds of formula II are generally commercially available or easily prepared by following known techniques.
The compounds of formula III can be prepared by reaction of a piperazme of formula V:
in which Ar is as defined above, with a compound of formula VIII:
Grpι-(CH2)n-T VIII
where Grpi is as defined above and T is a leaving group identical to or different from Grpi and preferably a better nucleofuge than Grpi,

A person skilled in the art knows in particular that a leaving group becomes increasingly labile as the corresponding negatively charged species resulting from the heterolytic cleavage of the bond increases in stability. In this particular instance, T~ must be more stable than Grpi" m order for T to be a better nucleofuge than Grpx.
According to a preferred alternative form of the invention, Grpi is a chlorine atom and T is a bromine atom.

The reaction of V with VIII is preferably carried out in a polar aprotic solvent chosen from those defined above, at a temperature of between 15 and 80°C, preferably between 15 and 35°C, for example at room temperature (20 to 25 °C) . Dimethylformamide is preferred, by way of solvents.
The reaction of the piperazme V with the compound VIII advantageously takes place in the presence of a base, such as potassium carbonate.
Another process of for the preparation of the compounds of formula I consist in reacting a piperazme of formula V
in which Ar is as defined above for the formula I, with a carboxyl derivative of formula VI
VI

in which n, X, Z and I are as defined above for the formula I, P2 is a protective group for a carboxyl functional group and Grp2 represents a leaving group. P2 may take any one of the meanings of Pi above. Just as for Pi, it is preferable for P2 to represent (Ci-Cβ) alkyl . Grp2 is a leaving group, the meaning of which is not critical according to the invention. Grp2 can usually represent a halogen atom, a (C6-Cιo) aryl- sulphonyloxy group, m which the aryl part is optionally substituted by one or more (Ci-Cβ) alkyl groups, or a (Cι-C6) alkylsulphonyloxy group, in which the alkyl group is optionally substituted by one or more halogen atoms.

The reaction of the piperazme V with the compound VI may be carried out in any one of the polar aprotic solvents defined above, preferably in acetomtrile. The yields and the kinetics of the reaction are markedly improved when the reaction is
carried out in the presence of a base and m particular in the presence of potassium carbonate.
The reaction may be carried out at a temperature of between 50 and 120°C, for example at reflux of the acetonitrile, when the latter acts as solvent.

By way of example, the piperazme of formula V is reacted with at least one equivalent of the compound of formula VI, m acetonitrile, in the presence of 1.5 to 3 equivalents of K2C03 with respect to the piperazme of formula V. The molar ratio of the compound of formula VI to the piperazme V is advantageously between 1 and 1.5, preferably between 1 and 1.2.

According to a preferred embodiment of the invention, the reaction of V with VI is carried out in the presence of an alkali metal iodide, such as potassium iodide. It can be of use to use up to 1 equivalent of alkali metal iodide with respect to the amount of piperazme V. Thus, the molar ratio of alkali metal iodide to the piperazme V may vary between 0.1 and 1.5 equivalents.
The reaction of the piperazme V with the compound VI results m a compound of formula VII:
P2OOC-CH2-- ->V->X-(CH2)n— VII
(Z)i

in which n, X, Z, Ar, l and P2 are as defined above, which compound is converted to a compound of formula I by deprotection of the carboxyl functional group. The operating conditions for the deprotection reaction will be easily determined by a person skilled in the art according to the nature of the P2 group.

When P2 represents (Cι-C6) alkyl, the deprotection can involve the saponification of the ester
functional group, for example by the action of dilute sodium hydroxide solution.
The compounds of formula V are commercially available or easily prepared from commercial compounds. The compounds of formula VI are easily prepared by reaction of a compound of formula IX
in which P2, X, Z and i are as defined above for the formula VI, with a derivative of formula X
A-(CH2)n-Grp2 X

where n and Grp2 are as defined above for the formula VI and A represents a leaving group identical to or different from Grp2 and preferably more nucleofugic than Grp2. According to a preferred embodiment of the invention, A is a bromine atom and Grp2 is a chlorine atom.
The operating conditions for this reaction will be easily determined by a person skilled in the art using his overall knowledge of organic chemistry.
The reaction of IX with X preferably takes place in a polar aprotic solvent in the presence of a base, at a temperature of between 15 and 120°C.

By way of example, the compound IX may be reacted with 1 to 4 equivalents, preferably 1.4 to 3 equivalents, of the derivative X in acetonitrile, as solvent, in the presence of 1.5 to 3.5 equivalents of K2C03 with respect to the amount of compound IX, at a temperature of between 40 and 120°C. The molar ratio of K2C03 to the compound X is advantageously between 0.8 and 1.2. The compounds of the invention are of use in the treatment of pathologies associated with insulin- resistance syndrome (syndrome X).
Insulin resistance is characterized by a reduction m the action of insulin (cf. Presse Medicale, 1997, 26 (No. 14), 671-677) and is implicated m a large number of pathological conditions, such as diabetes and more particularly non-msulm-dependent diabetes (type II diabetes or NIDDM) , dyslipidaemia, obesity, arterial hypertension and certain microvascular and macrovascular complications, such as atherosclerosis, retmopathies and neuropathies. Reference may be made, in this respect, to, for example, Diabetes, Vol. 37, 1988, 1595-1607, Journal of Diabetes and its Complications, 1998, 12, 110-119, or Hor . Res., 1992, 38, 28-32.
The compounds of the invention in particular exhibit a strong hypoglycaemic or hypol pidaemic activity.
Another subject-matter of the present invention is therefore pharmaceutical compositions comprising, as active principle, a compound according to the invention.

The pharmacuetical compositions according to the invention can be presented in forms intended for administration by the parenteral, oral, rectal, per- mucosal or percutaneous route. They will therefore be presented in the form of iniectable solutions or suspensions or multi-dose bottles, n the form of coated or uncoated tablets, of dragees, of capsules, including hard gelatin capsules, of pills, of cachets, of powders, of suppositories or of rectal capsules, of solutions or of suspensions, for percutaneous use, in a polar solvent, for permucosal use .

The excipients which are suitable for such administrations are derivatives of cellulose or micro- crystalline cellulose, alkaline earth carbonates, magnesium phosphate, starches, modified starches or lactose for the solid forms.

For rectal use, cocoa butter or polyethylene glycol stearates are the preferred excipients.
For parenteral use, water, aqueous solutions, physiological saline or lsotomc solutions are the most conveniently used vehicles.
The dosage can vary within wide limits accord- mg to the therapeutic indication and the administration route, as well as the age and the weight of the subject .
The invention therefore also relates to the use of the compounds of formula I in the preparation of medicaments intended for the treatment of diabetes.

The results of a pharmacological study will be given below.

Study of the antidiabetic activity in the rat The antidiabetic activity of the compounds of formula I by the oral route was determined on an experimental model of non-msulm-dependent diabetes induced in the rat by streptozotoc .
The model of non-msulm-dependent diabetes is obtained in the rat by a neonatal injection (on the day of bir hs of streptozotocm.

The diabetic rats used are 8 weeks old. The animals are kept, from the day of their birth to the day of the experiment, in an animal house at a regu- lated temperature of 21 to 22°C and are subjected to a fixed cycle of light (from 7 h to 19 h) and of darkness

(from 19 h to 7 h) . Their diet consisted of a maintenance diet; water and food were provided "ad libitum" , with the exception of the 2 hours of fasting preceding the tests, where food is withdrawn (post- absorptive state) .

The rats are treated oy the oral route, during the day, with the test product. Two hours after the final administration of the product and 30 minutes after anaesthetizing the animals with sodium pento- barbital [Nembutal ®> 300-μl blood sample is

These results show the effectiveness of the compounds of formula I in inducing a decrease the glycaemia in the diabetic animals.
Study of the hypolipidaemie activxty in the rat

The hypolipidaemie activity of the compounds of formula I by the oral route was determined on an experimental model of non-msulm-dependent diabetes induced m the rat by streptozotocm. The model of non-msulm-dependent diabetes is obtained in the rats by a neonatal injection (5 days after birth) of streptozotocm.

The diabetic rats used are 6 months old. The animals are kept, from the day of tneir oirth to the day of the experiment, in an animal house at a regulated temperature of 21 to 22°C and are subjected to a fixed cycle of light (from 7 h to 19 h) and of darkness (from 19 h to 7 h) .

Their diet consisted of a maintenance diet; water and food were provided "ab [sic] libitum", with the exception of the 18 hours of fasting preceding the withdrawals of the blood samples on which the lipid balances will be carried out.
The rats are treated by the oral route with the compound of Example 1 for 7 days. A 300-ul sample is withdrawn 18 h after the final administration of this compound.

The total cholesterol was quantitatively determined by the CHOE/CHOD/POD Tnnder method as an end point (Instrumentation Laboratory reagent [lacuna] on a Monarch plus analyser (Instrumentation Laboratory) .
The total triglyceπdes were quantitatively determined by the GPO/Trmder method as an end point (Sigma Diagnostic reagent) on a Monarch analyser (Instrumentation Laboratory) .
These results clearly demonstrate the hypolipidaemie activity of the compounds of the invention.
